newsitem.title: SPAIN: BASKETBALL-OLYMPIAKOS SLUMP TO DEFEAT IN SPAIN.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-OLYMPIAKOS SLUMP TO DEFEAT IN SPAIN.

text.p: Olympiakos, one of the big names of basketball, slumped to defeat in Spain on Thursday and face a tough new year in the EuroLeague.
The Greek club started the 10th and final round of the first phase in second place in group B and comfortably poised for an easier second phase schedule starting on January 9.

But Estudiantes of Madrid came from 35-40 down at halftime to win 87-78 and claim a top three place. With Cibona Zagreb winning 66-54 at leaders Teamsystem Bologna on Wednesday and Alba Berlin overcoming Charleroi of Belgium 79-69 , the 5-5 record of Olympiakos was not enough as they slipped to fifth.

Among their opponents next year will be Maccabi Tel Aviv who clinched third spot in Group A with a 71-65 victory over nearest rivals Ulker Spor of Turkey. Constantin Popa led the way for Maccabi with 18 points.
Popa was ably supported by some good outside shooting from Brad Leaf and Buck Johnson who both scored 14 points.

Orhun Ene was the dominant Ulker marksman with 21 points, but the Turks, who are expert at the three-point shot, also saw Haluk Yirdilim, and Dan Godfread strike from long range. Godfread finished with 14 points Also in Group A, Yann Bonato scored 20 points as former champions Limoges upset CSKA Moscow 83-66 to ensure they did not finish in last place.
Limoges, who made a disastrous start to the EuroLeague, ended up with four wins and six defeats in the first phase.
They finished ahead of Panionios of Greece, 79-86 losers against Stefanel Milan in Athens, in the standings.
CSKA, down 37-24 at halftime, never came to terms with Limoges' storming display which took the French side into a 28-8 lead after 12 minutes.
Despite the defeat, the Russians finished second in the group with a 6-4 record for 16 points, one behind Stefanel Milan.
There was drama in the Group C match in France with Villeurbanne snatching a dramatic 91-90 come-from-behind overtime victory against Barcelona.
Villeurbanne, who won seven of their 10 games, climbed to second in the group equal on points with Ljubljana of Slovenia and behind reigning champions Panathinaikos of Greece.
It was a sad result for Barcelona, beaten finalists last season, but struggling this time around with only four wins from their 10 matches.
The determined Catalans went 26-14 in front after 14 minutes although their lead was cut to three at haftime when they were just 35-32 up.
Estonian Arturas Karnishovas scored 18 points for Barcelona, who led by 10 points, 73-63 near the end of fulltime only to let Villeurbanne off the hook.
American Delaney Rudd, who scored 21 points altogether, made a three-point basket to bring the French team back into the match and the score was level at 74-74 at fulltime.
During the five-minute overtime period, Barcelona went into a 79-74 lead only to see it fall apart at the last gasp.
Now, like Olympiakos, they face a hard time in 1997 to get back on course in the race for the Final Four in Rome in April.
